summary: Catron County fire lookout tower and cabin built 1934 near Mangas, NM; NRHP-listed 1988; the 2020 chapter report marks it for restoration. Visitor access is unconfirmed.

facts.design: Aermotor MC-24 tower with a 12-by-12-foot wooden R3 low-sill cab and no catwalk

events.note: A fire lookout was on Mangas mountain in 1924, per a July 1924 Albuquerque Journal item as quoted by Forest Lookouts
Lookout Willis Bitmore (spelled that way on the source page) killed by lightning in a cabin on the mountain, per the 1924 newspaper item as quoted
Aermotor MC-24 tower with observation cab and a ground cabin; 30 feet per the 1934 USFS history, 31.6 feet per the register
Added to the National Register of Historic Places on January 28, 1988
Registered with the National Historic Lookout Register on January 2, 2006
2020 chapter report marks the lookout R, restoration or rehabilitation needed

notes_for_editor: Height: the record's height_m 9.1 (about 30 feet) matches the 1934 USFS history's 30-foot figure, but the register and the 2020 report give 31.6 feet (about 9.6 m). Not changed and not set in facts. The record's material steel refers to the tower; the register describes a wooden cab. Forest name is unresolved: the register says Apache, the 2020 report uses both Apache and Gila, and Wikipedia says Gila. The 1924 lookout's name is spelled Bitmore on the source page; the spelling is unverified. Living New Deal (which quotes the NRHP nomination form) returned HTTP 403 and was not read; the npgallery nomination text is not digitized. The 2020 report spells the listing Mangus Mtn. A recommendation sentence in the 2020 report near the Mangas photo was ambiguous about which lookout it covers, so it is not used. Access and current staffing are unknown.
